look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · Find the BRIGHT YELLOW five-lobed flower and examine the anthers: FOUR shorter yellow anthers plus ONE much LONGER CURVED, often dark-tipped anther. Then confirm the DEEPLY CUT leaves and sharp straw-colored prickles on stem, veins and the ENLARGING CALYX. The maturing berry is HIDDEN inside a spiny burr-like calyx, unlike the exposed yellow berries of western horsenettle and silverleaf nightshade. Buffalobur is typically an annual, not a spreading perennial.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Solanaceae/Solanum: alternate leaves, 5-parted rotate or star-shaped corollas, poricidal anthers, and berry fruits; prickles and stellate hairs occur in many species.
best_field_traits: alternate green deeply 1–2 times pinnately lobed leaves
FOUR shorter anthers plus ONE much longer curved darker-tipped anther
calyx covered in long straw-colored prickles; calyx becomes larger as fruit matures
berry concealed within enlarged, spiny burr-like calyx
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Most useful pairings are western horsenettle and silverleaf nightshade. Flower/anther asymmetry and enclosing prickly fruit calyx diagnose buffalobur more reliably than the mere presence of prickles.
morphology_keys.habit: Summer annual, erect to spreading and branching, often 0.2–0.6 m, frequently heavily armed with stiff yellowish prickles. Do not infer annuality from one photograph; use flowering/fruit structures to confirm.
morphology_keys.leaf: Simple ALTERNATE leaves, 1–2 times deeply pinnately lobed; lobes are often broad and rounded. Major leaf veins and petioles can also carry prickles. Inspect a mature leaf, not a newly unfolding one.
morphology_keys.flower: Five-lobed, fused BRIGHT YELLOW corolla, commonly about 1.5–3.5 cm across. Unlike the roughly equal yellow anthers of western horsenettle and silverleaf nightshade, buffalobur has four shorter yellow anthers and a conspicuously longer CURVED anther, often with a dusky reddish-purple tip. Anthers and style are DIFFERENT organs; don't label the slender style as the long anther.
morphology_keys.fruit: The calyx (joined sepals immediately behind the flower) becomes larger and densely prickly as fruit develops. It encloses the rounded fruit, creating a burr-like structure. Mature berry inside is typically small and brown/dry, not a large, freely exposed yellow berry.
morphology_keys.prickles: Check the calyx first, then the stems, petioles and main leaf veins for stiff straw-colored surface prickles. The prickly sphere in the photo is a CALYX enclosing the fruit, not the berry surface itself.
morphology_keys.habitat: Roadsides, disturbed soil, grazed ground and open dry sites. In the Hays/Edwards Plateau/Blackland Prairie encounter area, a familiar prickly summer annual; county-level native scoring remains deferred separately.
morphology_keys.management: Wear durable gloves and avoid gripping mature prickly burrs. If removing from a restoration bed, collect the bur-covered fruit before seed dispersal when practical, avoid disturbing desirable natives, and monitor seedlings. All parts should be treated as potentially toxic; never taste the fruit.
crew_field_sequence: 1 · WHOLE PLANT: Is this a branching, stiff-prickled herb with deeply dissected leaves, not a smooth broadleaf nightshade?
2 · FLOWER: Look for the YELLOW five-lobed corolla; identify the FOUR SHORT anthers and ONE LONG CURVED anther on the SAME flower.
3 · BUD/CALYX: Check the prickly green calyx immediately behind the flower; it expands as the fruit matures.
4 · FRUIT: Find the burr-like fruiting calyx that WRAPS around the berry; do not mistake the spiny calyx for a spiny berry.
5 · COMPARE: Purple flowers with exposed yellow berries favor western horsenettle or silverleaf; buffalobur has a yellow corolla and enclosing prickly calyx.

field_terms.Heterantherous: Having noticeably different anther forms or sizes on one flower. Buffalobur has four short and one long curved anther.
field_terms.Anther: Pollen-producing part of a stamen. The long dusky curved anther is NOT the pale style.
field_terms.Accrescent calyx: The sepals enlarge after flowering; in buffalobur they form a densely prickly enclosure over the berry.
field_terms.Pinnately lobed: Leaf indentations run inward toward the central midrib, leaving multiple side lobes.
field_terms.Prickle: Sharp surface growth on stem, vein or calyx, not a separate leaf or branch.
field_terms.Corolla: The flower's joined petals; here broad and bright yellow with five lobes.

field_matrix.leaf: Green, deeply lobed or dissected, prickly veins
field_matrix.flower: YELLOW corolla; ONE conspicuously long curved often dusky anther and four short
field_matrix.fruit: Berry HIDDEN by spiny enlarged calyx

field_matrix.flower: Lavender/purple or white; five roughly equal yellow anthers
field_matrix.fruit: Exposed yellow mature berry; small non-enclosing calyx

field_matrix.flower: Violet or white; five roughly equal yellow anthers
field_matrix.fruit: Exposed smaller yellow/orange berry; calyx does not enclose berry

not_reliable_alone: Prickles alone: other Solanum species can be prickly.
Deep leaf lobes alone: western horsenettle can also be deeply lobed.
Yellow flowers alone: confirm the UNEQUAL anther set and the accrescent prickly calyx.
Green unopened calyx alone: follow it to mature burs, or inspect a fully open flower.

items.label: 1 — Whole plant: leaves, flowers and developing burs
items.image_role: Open, branching habit with green deeply lobed leaves, yellow corollas and prickly enlarging calyces.
items.caption: In this real buffalobur plant, find the large green leaves cut into broad side lobes. Yellow flowers and ball-like developing burs occur on the SAME heavily armed plant. Compare western horsenettle's broad green lobed foliage but purple flowers.
items.why_it_matters: This overall view links the leaf outline to the yellow flower and prickly calyx rather than asking the crew to memorize color by itself.
items.creator: Dcrjsr

items.label: 2 — Flower close-up: four short anthers and one long anther
items.image_role: Yellow corolla, cluster of short anthers, one long curved darker anther, prickly green bud.
items.caption: The pale-yellow SHORT anthers gather near the flower center. The brownish CURVED ANTHER projects outward and is visibly longer. Do not confuse it with the pale, curled style beneath it. The hairy green calyx below/behind the corolla already carries sharp developing prickles.
items.why_it_matters: Unequal anthers distinguish this buffalobur flower from the approximately equal clustered anthers on western horsenettle and silverleaf nightshade.
items.creator: Dcrjsr

items.label: 3 — Prickly fruit enclosure: calyx versus berry
items.image_role: Maturing spiny enclosing calyces, surface prickles on stem and deeply lobed leaves.
items.caption: The round pale-green/yellowish SPINY burs are enlarged calyces surrounding the berry. The berry itself is hidden; we are NOT looking at a spiny berry surface. Stems and some leaf veins carry separate prickles. A western horsenettle or silverleaf ripe fruit would be visibly exposed.
items.why_it_matters: A densely prickly enlarged calyx around fruit is the best late-season separation from both purple-flowered look-alikes.
items.creator: Dcrjsr

items.label: 4 — LOOK-ALIKE: WESTERN HORSENETTLE, broad leaf and purple flower
items.image_role: Different Solanum species with large broadly lobed green leaves and purple flower.
items.caption: WESTERN HORSENETTLE, NOT BUFFALOBUR. Its green lobed foliage can look superficially similar, but flowers are lavender/purple and have five roughly equal yellow anthers. Mature fruit is exposed and yellow, not enveloped in an enlarged burr.
items.why_it_matters: Leaf lobes alone are not enough to split these prickly nightshades; use flower anthers and fruiting calyx.
items.creator: dsorenson

items.label: 5 — LOOK-ALIKE: SILVERLEAF NIGHTSHADE, narrow silvery leaves
items.image_role: Different Solanum species, silver-felted, usually narrow wavy leaves.
items.caption: SILVERLEAF NIGHTSHADE, NOT BUFFALOBUR. Check its dense gray/silvery felt and narrower leaves. Violet flowers have approximately equal yellow anthers; ripe berries are exposed rather than enclosed by a large thorny calyx.
items.why_it_matters: Use leaf pubescence, anther size symmetry, and fruiting-calyx architecture together.
items.creator: Alex Abair
